title: The people of the Atlas — content/atlas/people.json
description: Everyone in Wing III. Add a person by copying an existing { … } block.

name.description: Their name as shown in the Atlas.

domain.description: Which domain they sit in — an id from domains.json: found, market, mind, craft, recov or inner.

role.description: Who they are, in a line: "Executive coach; Art of Accomplishment".

corrected.description: The numbers of the colophon corrections that apply to this person, e.g. [17]. The drawer prints them, so a reader learns the entry was corrected and what changed. Add the number in the same change that runs `npm run correct`.

mentions.description: People on the Lives shelf that come up in your notes on this person — who they cite, work with, or name. Prints under 'How they connect' and in their drawer. Only what your notes say; never inferred.

note.description: What your notes say about it, in a sentence. A note, not a quotation.

take.description: Your take on what they teach — a sentence or two.

p.description: The principles they belong to — ids from principles.json. These draw their lines in the Atlas; with none, they float unconnected.

oneOf.description: A note: your line from listening, with no episode recorded. Prints as "Notes I kept · after <name>" and is labelled as not a quotation.

k.description: The line, as they said it. Verbatim, and short — a sentence or two, never a passage.

s.description: Where you heard it, precisely enough that a reader can go and check: "Founders #312, 14:20" or an episode URL.

kept.description: Lines you kept from them. Two shapes. { "k": "the line", "s": "the episode and timestamp" } prints as a quotation under 'Lines I kept' — verbatim, and only when you can say where it was said. A plain string prints as a note, 'after <name>', labelled as not a quotation. Upgrade a note by re-hearing it and adding its source; never guess one.
